id: title:Gilbert09:release the github batch reserve on quiet installations

review.posthog_relevance: Changes GitHub warehouse ingestion behavior: P1.F2.H4 and P1.F2.H3 implement a demand-responsive reserve policy that reduces the batch priority reserve from 30% to 10% for idle GitHub installations, while retaining full reserve for interactive demand. P1.F2.H3 adds Redis-backed demand markers and local memoization to support this policy. This could reduce warehouse backfill latency

observations.behavior: Adds a demand-responsive reserve policy for GitHub egress: when an installation has no recent interactive traffic, the BATCH priority reserve drops from 30% to 10% while an interactive-demand marker is absent; the marker is written on the attempt, not the outcome, and survives cache failures. The marker is cleared after 15 minutes of no activity. The policy uses a 10-second in-memo
observations.posthog_connection: Changes GitHub rate-limiting behavior: bulk warehouse backfills no longer waste 30% of hourly budget on idle accounts; interactive calls retain full reserve. This could reduce backfill latency and avoid unnecessary throttling while preserving user-facing availability.

observations.behavior: Adds helper functions and cache keys to record and check interactive demand, with a 10-second rewrite interval and 15-minute TTL. The marker is stored in Redis and also cached locally. Cache failures are treated conservatively: the marker is assumed present, preserving the full reserve.
observations.posthog_connection: Adds Redis-backed demand marker and local memoization. This could reduce Redis load while retaining demand state. Cache failure does not drop the reserve, preserving user-facing availability.

observations.behavior: Adds a 10-second in-process memo and 60-second rewrite interval, alongside a 15-minute Redis TTL. This could reduce Redis writes while retaining demand state.
